name: sol_token_fe_16
description: ERC20 transferFrom() incorrectly decreases allowance when caller is the token owner (sender)
question: The source file in `source` implements a transferFrom(sender, recipient, amount) function that unconditionally reduces the caller's or sender's allowance mapping even when msg.sender equals sender, causing the owner's own allowance to be needlessly consumed or underflow/revert when transferring their own tokens, and this statement excludes implementations that explicitly skip or bypass the allowance decrease when msg.sender == sender.
criteria: transferFrom(sender, recipient, amount) calls _approve(sender, msg.sender, allowance[sender][msg.sender] - amount) or similar without first checking if msg.sender == sender
transferFrom deducts from allowance[msg.sender][msg.sender] or allowance[sender][msg.sender] regardless of whether sender is the caller, leading to unnecessary allowance depletion
transferFrom reverts due to allowance underflow when sender calls transferFrom on their own address with amount exceeding their self-set allowance (which may be zero)
the allowance decrement logic in transferFrom lacks a branch or early return that skips decreasing allowance when sender == msg.sender
